scores.why: The sawn pair is the idea: one stone keeps the books apart. Rock in a block edges toward souvenir paperweight, but the split-pair logic and the Ember strata make it EARF's.
Perfect tint match, but the crystals are Sicilian under an Ethiopian name, and the provenance card has to admit it. A mineral under a dome is the most paperweight-like thing here.
Quiet and right: a core sample with a true sand bed reads as geology, not decoration. It is subtle enough that it needs the card to land, and loose sand in acrylic risks a souvenir-shop reading.
Wood in clear reads as the resin river-table trend and sits close to Nucleo's logs. KITSCH risk; organics also cut against the brand's own rule.
Dried plants in clear acrylic is the Lucite micro-cosmos and Rusak territory the prior art warns about, and it will fade. KITSCH: a pressed-flower keepsake.

The one edition whose name explains it: iron meteorite is the stand-in for the planet's core, set at the centre of a lamp called Core, its etched pattern lit from inside. Rare material, true story, nothing like it in the prior art.
A beach pebble in a weight is a gift-shop paperweight, and "bought, not taken" is a defence, not a story. KITSCH.

scores.line: Abraham. Frozen breath, twelve layers deep.
scores.why: It makes the lamination itself visible: a void at every bond line, stacked like lake ice. Strong Ice image. The name needs a footnote, and frozen methane bubbles are a well-worn photo trope, so the name should change before the object does.

scores.line: Fog bank. It rolls in from the bottom.
scores.why: The right habitat, but an edge-lit bubble field reads as generic LED acrylic signage. Fine as a finish, thin as an edition.
Beautiful and minimal, but a single controlled bubble is Steuben's, and an empty core is a weaker answer than Iron for the same product. Keep it as Iron's quiet sibling at most.

scores.line: Contour. Shasta at 2,000 m, drawn in air.
scores.why: Relief is already topography; one real contour in air is the panel's own logic, done in light. Abstract enough to stay clear of Ariel's figurative channels.

scores.line: Groove. The first second of Session 00.
scores.why: Sound into the weight that sits on the record is a good loop. But a drawn waveform is a gift-shop soundwave-print trope; it works only if it really is drawn as a groove, not as a waveform.

scores.line: Rain. It falls up the column.
scores.why: Literal habitat illustration, and bubble strings in a column read as an aquarium or bubble lamp. Thick Acid also hides it. KITSCH risk.

scores.line: Session 00. The tail of the first take.
scores.why: The story is strong and the material is real, but tape in a Lucite block reads as a commemorative embedment, one step from a deal toy. It needs the Smoke lamina and a form that is plainly a working weight.

scores.line: Stamper. The mirror that pressed it.
scores.why: Stampers are destroyed anyway; a shard with its grooves as a mirror, standing in the record stand, is sound made metal. Watch the framing so it never reads as a plaque.
Too small to see, even under a lens, and a relic in a corner is reliquary kitsch. An edition of one at best.

No foreign object at all: the factory's eight tints laid down in order, so the edition is EARF's own geology. The only nearby work is Marcelis's layered glass, and the ordered, dated offcut logic sets it apart.

scores.line: Drawing. The plan, over the thing.
scores.why: Paper laminated in clear is the tombstone, exactly. KITSCH/deal-toy.

notes: The strongest editions put the product's own logic inside it: a core in Core, a contour in Relief, the factory's tints in the core sample, the stamper in the record stand. Everything that is a foreign keepsake under clear (a pebble, oats, a burl, a drawing, a stylus) slides toward the paperweight and the tombstone, which is what the prior art warns against. Habitat specimens work only when the specimen is geology and the form does something with it (Iron, the sawn Cinder pair), not when it just displays it. Watch the sound pieces (Groove, Session 00 tape) for the soundwave-gift and commemorative-slab readings; their story is strong but their form is fragile. Fix the Dallol provenance mismatch, or rename it, before it reaches a card.
